Empirical Research Plan – “Economic Impacts of New Unionization in the Private Sector”

────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────
Chosen strategy: Sharp Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) around the 50-percent certification rule.

Justification
• The NLRB certifies a union when “yes” votes ≥ 50 % of valid ballots.  
• Firms whose elections are decided by 1–2 votes on either side are plausibly comparable in every respect except union status.  
• The discontinuous jump in the probability of becoming unionized at the 50 % threshold provides quasi-random assignment of treatment in a narrow bandwidth.  
• Cross-sectional RDD estimates the immediate effect; stacking multiple post-election years allows an event-style panel RDD to trace dynamic paths (optional extension).

────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control Definition
────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable
  Treat_i = 1 if the union won the certification election in firm i (union vote share ≥ 0.50), 0 otherwise.

Control group (counterfactual)
  Firms that held an election but where the union narrowly lost (union vote share < 0.50).

Running variable and cutoff
  m_i = (votes_for_union_i / total_valid_votes_i) – 0.50  
  Cutoff c = 0 (union certified if m_i ≥ 0).

Treatment timing / event date
  t = 0 is the fiscal year containing the election. Outcomes can be observed at t = 0 (immediate), t = +1, +2 … to study dynamics. Pre-treatment outcomes at t = –1, –2 test for balance.

────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Continuity of Potential Outcomes  
    In the absence of treatment, expected outcomes (employment, wages, productivity) vary smoothly in vote-share margin at m = 0.  
    Plausibility: Managers, workers, organizers cannot precisely control a handful of ballots; economic fundamentals drive neither vote tallies nor jump exactly at 50 %.

A2. No Manipulation of the Running Variable  
    Density of the vote-share margin is continuous at 0.  
    Plausibility: Secret ballots and NLRB monitoring reduce strategic mis-reporting. We will verify using McCrary density test.

A3. Precise Treatment at Cutoff (Sharp RDD)  
    Certification is deterministic at 50 %.  
    Plausibility: Statutorily true, aside from rare irregularities (<1 %). We will drop disputed cases.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA)  
    A firm’s outcome is unaffected by other firms’ election results within the estimation window.  
    Plausibility: Reasonable given geographically dispersed firms; we cluster SEs by election if firms appear multiple times.

A5. Local Linearity / Correct Functional Form  
    Within a narrow bandwidth around 0, the conditional expectation is well approximated by a linear function in m.  
    Plausibility: Will test robustness to alternative bandwidths and higher-order polynomials.

────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats & Remedies
────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Manipulation or sorting at cutoff  
    • Test: McCrary density and heaping patterns.  
    • Remedy: If imbalance detected, restrict to even narrower bandwidths; employ local randomization approach assuming discrete margins (±2 votes).

T2. Differential pre-trends / baseline differences  
    • Test: Plot pre-election outcomes against m; run placebo RDD on t = –1 variables.  
    • Remedy: Control for baseline covariates or use difference-in-discontinuities (post – pre) as robustness.

T3. Attrition or survival bias (post-election firm exit)  
    • Test: RDD on indicator of firm survival.  
    • Remedy: Inverse-probability weighting or Lee bounds; report intent-to-treat as main estimate.

────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# Required packages
library(data.table)    # fast data handling
library(fixest)        # regressions
library(rdrobust)      # RDD estimation
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading ------------------------------------------------------------
nlrb <- fread("nlrb_elections_1984_2001.csv")       # election data
firm  <- fread("firm_outcomes_panel.csv")           # outcomes by firm-year
data  <- merge(nlrb, firm, by = c("firm_id","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------------
data[, vote_share := votes_yes / votes_total]
data[, margin     := vote_share - 0.5]               # running variable
data[, treat      := as.integer(margin >= 0)]        # sharp RDD indicator
data[, post       := year >= election_year]          # optional DID layer
# Keep elections decided within ±0.20 vote-share initially
rdd_sample <- data[abs(margin) <= 0.20]

# 3. Main RDD estimation (local linear, conventional bandwidth) --------------
# Outcome example: log wage
rdd_main <- rdrobust(y = rdd_sample$log_wage,
                     x = rdd_sample$margin,
                     c = 0)          # defaults to optim. bandwidth

summary(rdd_main)

# 4. Covariate-adjusted RDD using fixest -------------------------------------
# Manual local linear regression with 10-percent bandwidth
bw <- 0.10
ll <- rdd_sample[abs(margin) <= bw]

est <- feols(log_wage ~ treat + margin | 0,
             data = ll, se = "hc3")
summary(est)

# 5. Robustness check: alternative bandwidth & placebo outcome ---------------
# (a) Half bandwidth
est_half <- feols(log_wage ~ treat + margin | 0,
                  data = rdd_sample[abs(margin) <= bw/2], se = "hc3")
# (b) Placebo RDD on pre-treatment log wage (t = -1)
placebo <- feols(lag_log_wage ~ treat + margin | 0,
                 data = ll, se = "hc3")

etable(est, est_half, placebo, tex = FALSE)

# 6. Graphical RDD plot -------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(rdd_sample[abs(margin) <= 0.20],
       aes(x = margin, y = log_wage)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", data = .[margin < 0], color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", data = .[margin >=0], color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Effect of Union Certification on Log Wages",
       x = "Vote-Share Margin (Union − 50%)", y = "Log Wage")
```

────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results (Prior Beliefs)
────────────────────────────────────────────
• Wages: Positive; unions bargain for higher compensation. Magnitude ≈ +3 % (≈ 0.03 log points) within two years.  
• Employment: Slightly negative due to higher labor costs and potential substitution to capital; magnitude ≈ –1 % to –2 %.  
• Productivity (revenue per worker): Ambiguous; possible small rise (+1 %) if efficiency gains offset wage increases.

────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: No sorting/manipulation at cutoff …………… 0.8  
C2: Covariate balance in narrow bandwidth ……… 1.0  
C3: Discontinuity in treatment probability …… 1.0  
C4: Robustness to bandwidth/polynomial choice … 0.8  
C5: No simultaneous policy discontinuities …… 0.9  

Average score: 0.9 – overall strong, but density and bandwidth testing remain critical.
